name: Ocean Triage Scheduler + Ingest Job Cleanup
purpose: Make the daily Ocean Context triage run automatically (today it is manual and last ran 2026-06-12), route triage findings somewhere an operator actually sees instead of only a ledger event plus a /context report file, and give operators tooling to inspect, retry, or abandon the 9 historical failed longhouse.ingest_jobs rows so the ingest queue is healthy. Hardens HANDOFF Priority 1 without redefining canonical Ocean boundaries: Bedrock remains the cloud-box support substrate that runs the triage ritual and exposes operator tooling; it is not the quorum engine.

canonicalBoundaries.oceanDaemon: Local runtime/body and execution authority. Owns local sessions, events, tools, provider execution, local filesystem/shell/destructive permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanLonghouse: Hive brain / coordination layer per ocean-os/docs/LONGHOUSE.md. Coordinates skills, SOPs, routines, MCP discovery, memory, subagents, quorum/council logic. Does not bypass daemon permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanBedrock: Cloud-box support substrate for shared files, context ingest, ledger/event store, Postgres/R2/Vectorize/KV, MCP-facing infrastructure, and coworker bootstrap. Does not redefine Longhouse.

currentState: Daily triage is fully implemented and live as a one-shot but is MANUAL: runOceanContextTriage (src/ocean-context.mjs:76) writes /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/YYYY-MM-DD.md, calls recordObjectWrite, and appends an ocean_context.triage.completed ledger event; it is reached via POST /api/v1/ocean-context/triage/daily (handleOceanContextTriage, src/server.mjs:1138, requiring write + /context/ocean-bedrock scope + CONFIDENTIAL clearance) and the HTTP-client script scripts/ocean-context-triage.mjs (npm run ocean:triage). There is NO scheduler deployed (HANDOFF.md sec 11/13 confirm: last ran 06-12). Findings reach NO operator surface beyond the ledger event and report file; thresholds are hardcoded in triageFindings (src/ocean-context.mjs:57-70): failedJobs>0 and queuedJobs>50. The ingest worker (scripts/ocean-ingest-worker.mjs) and claimNextIngestJob (src/metadata.mjs:118) only touch status='queued'; nothing inspects or requeues the 9 failed rows, and completeIngestJob can mark 'failed' but there is no un-fail/retry/abandon path. Railway cron (per use-railway docs) runs a service start command on a crontab and skips overlapping executions when the prior run is still Active, which fits the single-replica constraint.

phases.title: Choose and provision the triage scheduler mechanism
tasks: Adopt a DEDICATED Railway cron service (default decision) named ocean-bedrock-triage-cron over an in-server setInterval, because: (a) single-replica web service must not gain a 24/7 timer that double-fires on restart/redeploy; (b) Railway cron skips overlapping executions when the prior run is still Active, giving a free duplicate-run guard; (c) the existing scripts/ocean-context-triage.mjs already exits cleanly after one POST, satisfying Railway's 'exit on completion, leave no open resources' requirement.

Create the cron service in the SAME Railway project/environment as ocean-bedrock-production, start command 'npm run ocean:triage', Cron Schedule '0 6,18 * * *' UTC = TWICE DAILY at ~06:00 and ~18:00 UTC (a single cron expression that fires twice/day; operator may later shift the two hours). >=5min granularity and UTC-only per Railway cron docs. Do NOT point Nixpacks at a long-running server.

Set cron-service env: OCEAN_BEDROCK_URL=https://ocean-bedrock-production.up.railway.app and OCEAN_BEDROCK_TOKEN supplied via a Railway service variable (NOT committed). The token must be a scoped contributor token with write + /context/ocean-bedrock path scope + CONFIDENTIAL clearance, matching handleOceanContextTriage requirements (src/server.mjs:1139-1142). No raw secret in any repo artifact.
Add docs/HANDOFF.md sec 12-style runbook entry for the cron service (create, set schedule, set variable, redeploy) into the new docs/OCEAN-TRIAGE-OPS.md.

As a documented fallback ONLY (not the default), describe an in-server setInterval gated by OCEAN_TRIAGE_SCHEDULER=1 with a DB advisory-lock guard, to be used if a separate cron service is rejected; keep it OFF by default.
acceptance: Railway service ocean-bedrock-triage-cron exists in the production environment with start command 'npm run ocean:triage' and a saved Cron Schedule (verifiable via railway get_service_config / list_services).
The cron service has OCEAN_BEDROCK_URL and OCEAN_BEDROCK_TOKEN variables set, and neither token value nor any raw secret appears in git (grep of the repo for the token returns nothing).

A manual one-off run of the cron service produces a non-error deployment that exits, and a new /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/<today>.md report plus an ocean_context.triage.completed ledger event appear (verify via GET file + ledger read).

phases.title: Guard against duplicate / overlapping triage runs
tasks: Make a triage run idempotent PER SCHEDULED SLOT (NOT per calendar day, since the cron fires twice daily): key the marker source_sequence='triage:<dayStamp>:<slot>' where <slot> is the UTC hour bucket of the run (e.g. '06'/'18', or a configurable OCEAN_TRIAGE_SLOT). In runOceanContextTriage (src/ocean-context.mjs:76), before doing work, check for an existing ocean_context.triage.completed event with that per-slot source_sequence and, unless options.force is set, short-circuit returning {ok:true, skipped:'already-ran-this-slot', reportPath}. This lets the 06:00 and 18:00 runs BOTH proceed while still deduping an accidental re-fire within the same slot.
Thread a force flag through handleOceanContextTriage (src/server.mjs:1138) and scripts/ocean-context-triage.mjs (add --force) so an operator can still force a re-run.

Rely on Railway cron's built-in overlap skip (prior Active execution blocks the next) as the cross-process guard; document that the in-server fallback path must instead take a pg advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_lock) around the run for the same protection.
Ensure the short-circuit still works when the DB is reachable but the report file already exists, and that a forced re-run overwrites the same dated report path deterministically.
acceptance: The two scheduled slots (06:00 and 18:00 UTC) each produce their own ocean_context.triage.completed event (distinct per-slot source_sequence), but running the SAME slot twice without --force yields exactly one event for that slot and the second invocation returns skipped.
npm run ocean:triage -- --force re-runs and overwrites today's report, producing a second completed event only when forced.
Code review confirms no unguarded setInterval ships enabled by default.

phases.title: Route triage findings to an operator surface with thresholds
tasks: Add a notification step to runOceanContextTriage that fires only when actionable findings exist (any finding with severity in {high,medium}, or queuedJobs>OCEAN_TRIAGE_QUEUE_ALERT default 50, or failedJobs>OCEAN_TRIAGE_FAILED_ALERT default 0). Make the two thresholds env-configurable instead of the current hardcoded values in triageFindings (src/ocean-context.mjs:61-62).

OPERATOR DECISION (resolved 2026-06-14): the PRIMARY alert surface for this wave is the DIGEST FILE ONLY — no external notifier is provisioned. Implement src/notify.mjs as a thin dispatcher whose only ACTIVE channel is an operator digest written to /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/_alerts/<dayStamp>-<slot>.md (slot-stamped so the 06:00 and 18:00 runs do NOT clobber each other) and recorded via recordObjectWrite, so the operator has one place to look. Leave Telegram (OCEAN_TRIAGE_TELEGRAM_*) and generic-webhook (OCEAN_TRIAGE_WEBHOOK_URL) as DEFERRED, code-stubbed channels that stay OFF unless their env is set later — do NOT require any external credential this wave. Never log raw tokens.

Keep the existing ledger event and dated report as-is; the notification is additive. Include in the alert: dayStamp, the severity-sorted findings list, and key counts (failedJobs, queuedJobs, pendingChunks, failedSyncRuns).
Make notification failures non-fatal to the triage run (catch + record a low-severity note) so a flaky Telegram/webhook never blocks the report/ledger write.

Document the chosen default surface and env vars in docs/OCEAN-TRIAGE-OPS.md; record 'Telegram vs webhook vs dashboard file as the primary operator surface' as an open decision if the operator has not committed to one.
acceptance: A triage run with actionable findings writes /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/_alerts/<today>-<slot>.md and records it as an object (verify file GET + longhouse.objects row); the 06:00 and 18:00 digests coexist without clobbering.
OCEAN_TRIAGE_QUEUE_ALERT and OCEAN_TRIAGE_FAILED_ALERT change which findings are emitted (manual check: set OCEAN_TRIAGE_FAILED_ALERT=100 and confirm a 9-failed-jobs DB no longer triggers an alert).
The deferred Telegram/webhook channels stay inert when their env is unset (no external call attempted), and a digest-write error is non-fatal (report + ledger event still produced).

phases.title: Inspect, retry, and abandon failed ingest jobs
tasks: Add metadata helpers in src/metadata.mjs: listFailedIngestJobs({limit}) (SELECT id, job_type, status, virtual_path, attempts, max_attempts, error, updated_at FROM longhouse.ingest_jobs WHERE status='failed' ORDER BY updated_at DESC), requeueIngestJob(id, {resetAttempts}) (UPDATE ... SET status='queued', locked_by=null, locked_at=null, run_after=now(), attempts = CASE WHEN resetAttempts THEN 0 ELSE attempts END, error=null), and abandonIngestJob(id, reason) (UPDATE ... SET status='cancelled', error=reason) — using only states already in the db/001 CHECK constraint (queued|running|done|failed|cancelled), so NO new migration is required.

Create scripts/ocean-failed-jobs.mjs (npm run ocean:jobs) with subcommands: list (default), retry <id|--all> [--reset-attempts], abandon <id|--all> --reason <text>, and inspect <id> (prints the full row incl. error + payload). Default to a dry-run/print for --all retry/abandon and require an explicit --yes to mutate, matching the cautious posture of the destructive-action gates in the week-one workflow.
Wire abandon/retry actions to also append a ledger event (e.g. ocean_context.ingest.job_requeued / job_abandoned) so operator actions on the queue are auditable in the same timeline as triage.

Run the new tool against prod to triage the 9 historical failed rows: inspect each, retry the ones whose error is transient (so the existing worker scripts/ocean-ingest-worker.mjs can pick them up since claimNextIngestJob selects status='queued'), and abandon the ones whose virtual_path/object no longer exists; record the disposition in docs/OCEAN-TRIAGE-OPS.md.
Have triage surface a follow-up: extend the ingest finding in triageFindings to note when failed jobs are stale (failed and not retried for N days) so the cleanup loop is self-reminding.
acceptance: npm run ocean:jobs list prints the failed rows with id/job_type/virtual_path/error; npm run ocean:jobs inspect <id> prints the full error + payload.

After running retry/abandon on the 9 rows, SELECT count(*) FROM longhouse.ingest_jobs WHERE status='failed' returns 0, with each row now either 'queued' (and subsequently processed to 'done' by the worker) or 'cancelled'.
Each retry/abandon action produced a corresponding ledger event (verify via ledger read filtered to ingest.job_* event types), and --all without --yes performed no mutation (dry-run only).

launchDefinitionOfDone: A dedicated Railway cron service ocean-bedrock-triage-cron runs 'npm run ocean:triage' TWICE DAILY ('0 6,18 * * *' UTC) in the production environment, exits cleanly each run, and is not the long-running web service.
The cron service authenticates with a scoped contributor token (write + /context/ocean-bedrock + CONFIDENTIAL) delivered via a Railway variable, with no raw secret in the repo.

Triage is idempotent per scheduled slot (the 06:00 and 18:00 runs each produce one event; a re-fire within a slot dedupes without --force) and overlapping runs are prevented via Railway cron overlap-skip.

Actionable triage findings reach the operator via a slot-stamped /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/_alerts/<day>-<slot>.md digest object (the chosen primary surface; Telegram/webhook deferred OFF); thresholds for queued/failed jobs are env-configurable.
npm run ocean:jobs can list/inspect/retry/abandon failed ingest jobs, defaulting to dry-run for bulk ops and emitting ledger events for actions.
The 9 historical failed longhouse.ingest_jobs rows are dispositioned so SELECT count(*) WHERE status='failed' returns 0 (each retried-and-done or cancelled).
docs/OCEAN-TRIAGE-OPS.md exists and HANDOFF sec 11/13 + OCEAN-CONTEXT limits are updated to reflect the deployed scheduler and tooling.
Security review confirms no token/secret leakage in repo/logs/report/digest, non-destructive defaults on bulk job ops, and a documented rollback.
openDecisions: RESOLVED (operator, 2026-06-14): primary alert surface = the /context/ocean-bedrock/triage/_alerts/<day>-<slot>.md digest file ONLY; Telegram/webhook deferred OFF (no external notifier secret this wave).
RESOLVED (operator, 2026-06-14): cadence = twice daily, cron '0 6,18 * * *' UTC (~06:00 and 18:00); operator may later shift the two hours.

Whether to keep the in-server setInterval fallback (OCEAN_TRIAGE_SCHEDULER flag + advisory lock) in the codebase at all, or rely solely on the dedicated cron service. Default keeps it present but OFF.
Retry policy for the 9 failed rows: blanket requeue-with-reset-attempts vs per-row inspection. Spec defaults to per-row inspect-then-decide.
Whether to later promote the file-based alert digest into a real operator dashboard surface (out of scope for this wave; the longhouse data-plane router is wave 2).
risks: Single-replica constraint: an in-server setInterval scheduler would double-fire on redeploy/restart and the token registry is volume-JSON (src/auth.mjs) safe only for one replica; this is why the spec mandates a separate cron service and same-day idempotency rather than an in-process timer.
Railway cron has >=5min granularity, UTC-only, and a few-minutes imprecision; not suitable if sub-day or precise-time triage is later required.

The cron service needs a live, scoped token; if the token is mis-scoped (missing /context/ocean-bedrock or CONFIDENTIAL clearance) the run 403s. Token rotation must be handled via Railway variables, not committed.

Retrying a failed ingest job whose underlying file/object no longer exists (e.g. deleted from state.filesRoot) will just re-fail in processIngestJob (src/metadata.mjs:150) since file ops resolve a single hardcoded local disk root; such rows should be abandoned, not retried.

With digest-only chosen, NO new external notifier secret is introduced this wave (the deferred Telegram/webhook stubs need no creds while OFF), removing that leak surface. If those channels are enabled later, treat their tokens as new secrets (non-fatal notifier, never log values).

Ordering note for openDecisions: this track is assigned firingOrder=1 with dependsOnWorkflows=[] as instructed and that holds, because nothing here requires the longhouse data-plane router (wave 2) or source runners (wave 3). The failed-job retry path does depend on the existing local-disk worker, so some of the 9 rows may only be cleanable by abandon until wave-2 mounts land; this is a soft dependency captured here, not a change to firing order.
